To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we found that the most frequent user actions on Web mail are read, reply, and delete, and that (2) we can predict the actions of a user on an incoming message with a high degree of accuracy, which is important to help users manage their email inboxes.

(1) we can predict actions on messages with a precision of up to 40%; (2) we can predict important messages (i.e. messages that will be read or replied) with a recall of 90% and a precision of up 30%.
we can predict actions of users on their email messages with an accuracy of 40%, which is an encouraging level for a user assistance application.

the question: "What could you do with your email messages?".
the question of how we can assist users in processing their email messages.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have proposed an effective framework for predicting user actions on Web mail.

we have developed and evaluated a new learning framework that is able to predict multiple actions on email messages with a high level of accuracy, and which can be used to help users manage their inboxes.
, with our framework and our results, we have provided a strong basis to the community for designing new user experiences to assist users in processing their inboxes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is now possible to predict the actions of users on their email messages with reasonable accuracy, and that this can be done with a privacy preserving approach.

, with the help of machine learning techniques, we can now help users process their mail inboxes by predicting the actions they are most likely to conduct on their received messages, with a high recall and a good precision.
it is now possible, with a reasonable level of accuracy, to predict the most important actions that users conduct on Web email, with a large-scale experiment, and to provide assistance accordingly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by analyzing the actions of users on their messages, we can learn to predict their actions in the future and help them process their email more efficiently.
, by learning from the users' actions, we can predict with high accuracy the actions they are likely to take, and thus provide a better user experience.
, by learning to predict the actions of users on email messages, we can provide a new ground to invent new user experiences that assist users in processing their inboxes.
